name: Indian Independence
description: The first postage stamp issued by independent India, carrying the national flag.
story: Issued on 15 August 1947, the day independence took effect, this 3½ annas stamp was the first to carry the flag of a free India. It opened the postal history of a country now mailing its own stamps.
designNote: The tricolour with the dharmachakra at its centre, engraved in the flat, even lines of the period.

name: Constitution of India
description: 2 annas stamp issued on the occasion of India being proclaimed a republic.
story: Issued on 26 January 1950, when the Constitution came into force and India became a sovereign democratic republic. The 2 annas value kept it in everyday use, so the symbols of the new state travelled on ordinary mail.
designNote: A ceremonial layout in the engraved monochrome style of India's early republican issues.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
file: File:Stamp of India - 1948 - Colnect 141344 - Mahatma Gandhi.jpeg
description: India's first postage stamp portraying Mahatma Gandhi.
story: India's first stamp to carry the portrait of the man who led the independence movement. It was issued in 1948 and became one of the most collected Indian issues of the twentieth century.
designNote: A plain engraved portrait, deliberately unadorned: the subject is the face, not the frame.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
file: File:Stamp of India - 1964 - Colnect 371661 - Mourning of Jawaharlal Nehru 1889-1964.jpeg
description: A mourning issue for Jawaharlal Nehru, 1889-1964.
story: Jawaharlal Nehru died on 27 May 1964. The post office issued this memorial stamp the same year, printed by the Security Printing Press in Nasik, so the country could mark the passing of its first prime minister on the mail.
designNote: Memorial portrait and dates set with the restrained typography of a mourning issue.

name: Bengal Tiger
file: File:Stamp of India - 1963 - Colnect 238978 - Tiger Panthera tigris.jpeg
description: The Bengal tiger, India's national animal, on a 1963 definitive.
story: One of a 1963 set of animal definitives printed for everyday postage, putting India's national animal into regular circulation. Definitives stay on sale for years, which is why wildlife became a staple of Indian albums.
designNote: Intaglio hatching builds the striped coat in fine parallel lines.

name: Indian Elephant
file: File:Stamp of India - 1963 - Colnect 155176 - Asian or Asiatic Elephant Elephas maximus.jpeg
description: The Asian elephant, long central to Indian life, in the 1963 animal set.
story: The Asian elephant has carried people, timber and royalty in India for centuries. Here it joins the 1963 set of animal definitives that was meant for everyday postage rather than the album alone.
designNote: A single animal study framed by the plain border of a definitive value.

name: Indian Peacock
file: File:Stamp of India - 1973 - Colnect 372313 - Common Peacock Pavo cristatus.jpeg
description: The common peacock, declared India's national bird in 1963, on a 1973 issue.
story: The peacock was declared India's national bird in 1963, and this 1973 stamp continued the wildlife definitives that had begun a decade earlier with the tiger and the elephant.
designNote: The tail fanned behind the bird, engraved so the eye-spots read as texture.

name: Aryabhata Satellite
file: File:Stamp of India - 1975 - Colnect 372793 - Aryabhata Satellite.jpeg
description: India's first satellite, launched in 1975.
story: Named after the ancient Indian mathematician and astronomer, Aryabhata was India's first satellite, launched in 1975. The stamp marks the moment Indian engineering entered orbit.
designNote: The satellite drawn against a plain ground, the orbital path implied rather than drawn.

name: Rohini Satellite
file: File:Stamp of India - 1981 - Colnect 505879 - Launch of Rohini Satellite.jpeg
description: Stamp marking the launch of India's Rohini satellite.
story: Rohini was the satellite carried by India's Satellite Launch Vehicle, developed at Thumba. This 1981 issue celebrates a rocket programme built and fired from Indian soil.
designNote: Issued in the flat commemorative style of India's science issues, with one clear focal device.

name: Taj Mahal
file: File:Stamp of India - 2004 - Colnect 158552 - Taj Mahal.jpeg
description: The Taj Mahal on a 2004 World Heritage definitive.
story: Built by Shah Jahan at Agra, the Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most reproduced monuments in philately. India's World Heritage definitives put it back on everyday mail in 2004.
designNote: The dome and minarets reduced to clean architectural linework.

name: Asian Games Delhi
file: File:Stamp of India - 1982 - Colnect 169301 - IX Asian Games Delhi 1982 - Football.jpeg
description: Football stamp from India's issue for the IX Asian Games, Delhi 1982.
story: Delhi hosted the ninth Asian Games in 1982 and India Post released a set of issues for the event, one sport per stamp. This entry is the football stamp from that series.
designNote: A single sport per value, drawn as a compact pictorial in the set's shared layout.

name: Sachin Tendulkar
description: Issued for Sachin Tendulkar's 200th Test match in 2013.
story: Sachin Tendulkar's 200th Test was a record for matches played in international cricket, and India Post marked it with this issue. It is among the rare Indian stamps of a living sportsperson.
designNote: A portrait-led commemorative in India Post's standard single-colour format.

name: Penny Black
file: File:Penny Black, world's first postage stamp, 1840.jpg
description: The world's first adhesive postage stamp, issued in 1840.
story: Issued on 1 May 1840 and valid for postage from 6 May of that year, the Penny Black made the sender rather than the receiver pay for a letter. One penny covered a letter anywhere in Britain.
designNote: A profile of Queen Victoria after William Wyon's medal, cut in fine line engraving.

name: Penny Red
description: The 1841 red-brown successor to the Penny Black.
story: The Penny Black's black ink cancelled badly, so Britain switched to a red-brown stamp in 1841. The design stayed the same, and with small changes the Penny Red stayed on sale until 1879 - almost forty years of everyday postage.
designNote: The same Wyon portrait, now printed in red-brown so cancellations read cleanly.

name: Coronation of Elizabeth II
description: The 1s 3d stamp issued for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II.
story: Issued in June 1953 for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II, one of a set of commemorative values designed by Edmund Dulac. Coronation stamps were among the first British issues bought as souvenirs rather than for postage alone.
designNote: A crowned profile inside a ceremonial border, in a tall narrow format.

name: Commonwealth Games 1958
description: 3d stamp for the 1958 British Empire and Commonwealth Games in Cardiff.
story: The 1958 Games were held in Cardiff - still the only time they have been staged in Wales. This 3d stamp carries the Welsh dragon alongside the event name, tying a British issue to a specific host city.
designNote: The Welsh dragon set against the numerals of the Games, printed in a single strong colour.

name: London 1948 Olympics
description: British stamp for the XIV Olympic Summer Games, London 1948.
story: London hosted the 1948 Games, the first after the Second World War, with almost no new venues built. This stamp, titled Speed, sets King George VI beside the Olympic rings and a stylised globe.
designNote: Speed rendered as a streamlined device before a globe, with a side portrait of the King.

name: George Washington 1847
description: The 10 cent Washington from the first United States postage stamp issue.
story: The United States issued its first stamps on 1 July 1847, and the 10 cent value carried George Washington. Prepaid postage was still new in the States - the act that enabled the issue had passed only the year before.
designNote: An engraved portrait framed in scrollwork, in the manner of the 1847 issue.

name: Spirit of '76
description: A triptych of stamps reproducing Archibald Willard's painting Spirit of '76.
story: Issued for the United States bicentennial in 1976, this joined block of three stamps reproduces the 1876 painting Spirit of '76 - the drummers and fife player of the Revolution - across one continuous picture.
designNote: Three se-tenant stamps whose combined picture follows the painting's diagonal march.

name: Emancipation Proclamation
description: 5c stamp marking the centenary of the Emancipation Proclamation.
story: Released on 16 August 1963, the hundredth anniversary of the Emancipation Proclamation, on the opening day of the Century of Negro Progress Exposition in Chicago. Designer Georg Olden broke a black chain against blue - one of the boldest American stamp designs of its decade.
designNote: A severed chain link, graphic and flat, with the date set in clean modern type.

name: John F. Kennedy
description: The 5 cent memorial stamp for President John F. Kennedy.
story: Issued on 29 May 1964, on what would have been Kennedy's forty-seventh birthday, with first-day cancellations in Boston. It carries lines from the inaugural address of 20 January 1961.
designNote: The portrait beside the quotation, engraved in a restrained memorial style.

name: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
description: 10c stamp issued for the first crewed Moon landing in 1969.
story: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969. The 10 cent stamp followed within weeks, engraved by the Bureau of Engraving and Printing - one of the fastest commissions in American philatelic history.
designNote: The lunar module and a lone figure on the surface, cut in fine engraved line.

name: Ceres
description: France's first postage stamp: 20 centimes in black, issued in 1849.
story: Put on sale on 1 January 1849, the first French stamp shows the goddess Ceres after a design by Jacques-Jean Barre. Early impressions were printed in black on yellow paper, a combination collectors still look for.
designNote: A classical profile of Ceres with her wheat crown, engraved in the official style of the period.
wikipedia: Postage stamps and postal history of France

name: Louis Pasteur
file: File:France 1923 YT 176 Mi 157 stamp (Type 'Pasteur'. Louis Pasteur (1822-1895), French chemist and microbiologist) small resolution cancelled.jpg
description: France's 1923 stamp in honour of Louis Pasteur, 1822-1895.
story: Pasteur died in 1895 and France honoured him with this engraved type in 1923, part of a run of scientific and national figures used on French issues of the period.
designNote: A formal portrait in the engraved 'type Pasteur' style by George Henri Prudhomme.

name: Semeuse
description: 30 centimes red of the Sower definitive, printed in 1922.
story: The Sower - a peasant woman scattering seed - was designed by Louis-Eugene Mouchon and became the face of French postage for decades. This 30 centimes red of 1922 is a plain working example of the design in daily use.
designNote: The walking figure mid-stride, seed falling from her hand, framed by the value tablets.

name: Paul Cézanne
description: France's 1939 commemorative issue for Paul Cézanne.
story: France honoured Paul Cézanne in 1939, the centenary of his birth at Aix-en-Provence, in a series that gave postage stamps to the country's painters.
designNote: A portrait in the sober engraved manner used for the artist commemoratives.

name: Lazare Hoche
description: French issue of 1948 honouring General Lazare Hoche, 1768-1797.
story: Lazare Hoche led republican armies while still in his twenties and died at twenty-eight. France placed him on a 1948 stamp in a series of national figures issued in the years after the war.
designNote: An engraved portrait in uniform, set with the plain lettering of the period's commemoratives.

name: Sachsen Dreier
description: The Saxony 'Dreier' of 1850, among the first stamps of the German states.
story: Before Germany existed as a single country, its states printed their own postage. Saxony's 3 Pfennige of 1850 - the Dreier - is one of the earliest of these, decades before the empire's post took over.
designNote: A numeral and coat of arms on a small square of tinted paper, engraved by J. B. Hirschfeld.

name: Brandenburg Gate
description: West German issue of 1966 showing the Brandenburg Gate.
story: The Brandenburg Gate, built between 1789 and 1791, stood in the closed border strip after 1961. West Germany's 1966 stamp turned it into a symbol of a divided country and, in time, of reunion.
designNote: The gate in side elevation with the quadriga above, in the engraved style of Deutsche Bundespost architecture values.

name: German Reunification
description: Stamp issued for German reunification on 3 October 1990.
story: Germany was reunified on 3 October 1990, and the post issued a special value, Deutsche Einheit, in the same year - an issue bought in large numbers as a souvenir of the moment.
designNote: A compact commemorative built around the date and the words Deutsche Einheit.

name: Munich 1972 Olympics
file: File:Stamps of Germany (BRD), Olympiade 1972, Ausgabe 1970, 30 Pf.jpg
description: 30 Pfennig issue of 1970 for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich.
story: West Germany released its Olympic values two years ahead of the Games. This 30 Pfennig stamp of 1970 uses the Glyptothek, Munich's classical sculpture museum, as its image for the 1972 Games.
designNote: Classical architecture carrying the Games' identity, in the flat engraved style of the Olympic set.

name: 100 Years of German Football
description: Germany's first round stamp, issued on 13 January 2000 for 100 years of the DFB.
story: The German Football Association turned a hundred in 2000, and Deutsche Post marked it on 13 January with MiNr 2091 - the first circular stamp ever issued in Germany, printed in sheets of ten.
designNote: A round die-cut design instead of the usual rectangle, the feature the issue is remembered for.

name: Mona Lisa
description: West German stamp for the 500th birthday of Leonardo da Vinci, reproducing the Mona Lisa.
story: Leonardo was born in 1452. Deutsche Bundespost marked his 500th birthday in 1952 with the Mona Lisa, a painting by then among the most reproduced in the world.
designNote: The portrait reduced to the size of a small engraved window, in monochrome.

name: Dragon
description: Japan's first postage stamps, issued in 1871.
story: Japan's Dragons of 1871 were the country's first postage stamps, printed during the decade in which the modern postal service was being built from scratch. Letter writing and stamp design both changed quickly in the years that followed.
designNote: The imperial dragon engraved in a rectangular frame, printed in dark brown.
wikipedia: Postage stamps and postal history of Japan

name: Cherry Blossom
description: 10 yen definitive of 1961 showing somei-yoshino blossom.
story: This 10 yen definitive of 1961 shows the somei-yoshino, the variety that lines Japan's parks and riverbanks in spring. Blossom viewing is an annual national ritual, which is why the subject keeps returning to Japanese postage.
designNote: A flowering branch in the spare, single-colour style of Japan's definitives.

name: Tokyo 1964 Olympics
file: File:1964 Olympics judo stamp of Japan.jpg
description: Japanese stamp for the 1964 Tokyo Games, showing judo.
story: The 1964 Tokyo Games were the first held in Asia. Judo joined the Olympic programme that year, giving Japan's own martial art a world stage on home soil.
designNote: Two figures mid-throw, drawn with the clean linework of the Games' Japanese philatelic set.

name: Nikko Toshogu
description: 45 yen stamp of 1952 showing the shrine buildings at Nikko.
story: The Toshogu shrine at Nikko is the mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu, its buildings covered in carved and gilded detail. A 45 yen definitive put that architecture into everyday circulation in 1952.
designNote: Ornate shrine detail flattened into a single-colour engraved vignette.

name: Mount Fuji
description: Blue 10 sen definitive showing Mount Fuji as seen from Mishima.
story: Japan's 1936 definitives used views of Fuji on low, widely used values; this one shows the mountain from Mishima. No outline in Japanese philately is repeated more often than the cone of Fuji.
designNote: The mountain's cone above a foreground plain, in a single blue ink.

name: Large Dragons
description: The 1 candareen Large Dragon stamp of 1878, China's first postage stamps.
story: The Large Dragons went on sale in 1878, when the Imperial Maritime Customs ran China's new post. Three values were printed, and the series is the starting point for every Chinese collection.
designNote: The imperial dragon coiled within a printed frame, engraved for the 1 candareen value.

name: Giant Panda
file: File:Panda on stamp of China Post, 1973 60.jpg
description: China Post issue of 1973 featuring the giant panda.
story: The giant panda is a national symbol of China and a fixture of international conservation campaigns. This 1973 issue gives the animal a whole stamp to itself.
designNote: Soft tonal blocks suggest the animal's thick black and white markings.

name: Monument to the People's Heroes
file: File:Ji47, Monument to the People's Heroes, 1958.jpg
description: 1958 commemorative for the Monument to the People's Heroes in Beijing.
story: The obelisk in Tiananmen Square was completed in 1958 and honours those who died for the revolution since 1840. This issue is number Ji47 in China's commemorative catalogue.
designNote: The obelisk drawn upright against a plain sky, in the engraved style of China's commemoratives.

name: Qu Yuan
description: 1953 stamp for the ancient Chinese poet Qu Yuan.
story: Qu Yuan, a poet of the Warring States period whose verses survive in the Songs of Chu, is remembered each year at the Dragon Boat Festival. In 1953 China gave him a place in its commemorative series.
designNote: A robed figure in the flat engraved portrait style of China's early commemoratives.

name: Founding of the People's Republic
file: File:Ji4, 4-1, Commemoration of the Founding of the People's Republic of China, 1950.jpg
description: 1950 commemorative for the founding of the People's Republic of China.
story: The People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 October 1949, and this four-stamp issue followed in 1950. It is catalogue number Ji4, the first commemorative set of the new state's postal service.
designNote: A formal commemorative layout in a single engraved colour, typical of Ji-series issues.

name: Bull's Eye
description: Brazil's first postage stamp, the 30 réis Bull's Eye of 1843.
story: Brazil issued its first stamps on 1 August 1843, only the second country in the world to do so after Britain. The dark design shows no monarch, just a printed numeral inside an ellipse that collectors soon nicknamed the Bull's Eye.
designNote: A shaded oval around the numeral: all engraving, no portrait.

name: Rio Carnival
file: File:Stamp of Brazil - 1967 - Colnect 263108 - Rio Carnival.jpeg
description: Brazilian issue of 1967 for the Rio Carnival.
story: Rio de Janeiro's carnival grew from the street masquerades of the nineteenth century into a spectacle broadcast around the world by the 1960s. Brazil Post marked it with a stamp in 1967.
designNote: Pictorial design printed in strong flat colour, characteristic of Brazil's commemorative issues.

name: FIFA World Cup 1970
file: File:Stamp of Brazil - 1970 - Colnect 213992 - 9th FIFA s World cup - Mexico.jpeg
description: Brazilian stamp for the 1970 World Cup in Mexico.
story: The ninth World Cup, held in Mexico, was won by Brazil - a third title that let them keep the Jules Rimet trophy for good. This issue shows that trophy with the host and home maps.
designNote: The trophy set above a map device, in the flat pictorial style of the issue.

name: Harpy Eagle
file: File:Stamp of Brazil - 1968 - Colnect 196476 - Harpy Eagle Harpia harpyja.jpeg
description: Brazilian issue of 1968 featuring the harpy eagle.
story: The harpy eagle is one of the largest birds of prey in the Americas, hunting through the canopy of the Amazon forest. This 1968 stamp belongs to Brazil's long run of bird and animal issues.
designNote: The bird's crested head held in profile, engraved to keep detail at stamp size.

name: Brasília
file: File:Stamp of Brazil - 1960 - Colnect 189473 - Plan of Brasilia.jpeg
description: Brazilian stamp of 1960 for the new capital, Brasília.
story: Brasília was inaugurated on 21 April 1960, built from scratch on the inland plateau as the capital of a country whose people lived almost entirely along the coast. Oscar Niemeyer and Lúcio Costa designed its buildings and plan.
designNote: The planned city's layout reduced to a graphic plan within the stamp frame.

name: Kangaroo and Map
description: Australia's first stamp issue of 1913, showing a kangaroo over the map.
story: Australia's first stamps arrived in 1913, replacing the separate state issues. Debate over showing a monarch or an animal was settled in favour of the kangaroo and the map: a deliberate statement about distance and fauna.
designNote: The animal standing over an outline of the continent, a small design with a strong silhouette.
wikipedia: Postage stamps and postal history of Australia

name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
description: Australian stamp of 1932 for the Sydney Harbour Bridge.
story: The bridge opened in March 1932 after six years of construction, spanning the water that had divided Sydney's two shores. Australia's 1932 pictorial set put the structure into the country's album that same year.
designNote: A literal view of the bridge, engraved as an architectural record for a commemorative value.

name: Melbourne 1956 Olympics
description: Australian stamp for the XVI Olympic Games, Melbourne 1956.
story: The 1956 Games were the first held in the southern hemisphere, staged in Melbourne from late November into December. This commemorative was issued for the occasion as one of the Melbourne Games values.
designNote: A commemorative value with the Games' name and date set around a central device.

name: Superb Lyrebird
description: 1932 Australian stamp showing the superb lyrebird (Scott #141).
story: The superb lyrebird lives in the forests of south-eastern Australia and has among the most elaborate songs and displays of any songbird. It appeared in the 1932 pictorial set alongside the Sydney Harbour Bridge.
designNote: The bird's tail drawn as a fan of fine engraved lines.

name: Italian Ceres
description: 1862 Ceres issue, regarded by some catalogues as the first stamp of unified Italy.
story: Printed in Turin by Francesco Matraire, this Ceres follows the Sardinian design used before unification. Catalogued as Michel 9, it is counted by some catalogues as the first postage stamp of the Kingdom of Italy.
designNote: The classical profile of Ceres, drawn as a close relation of the Sardinian original.

name: Egypt's First Stamps
description: 20 para stamp from Egypt's first issue of 1866.
story: Egypt's first postage stamps were released in 1866 under the khedivate. This 20 para value belongs to that opening set, printed before the country's later pictorial issues became famous for ancient monuments.
designNote: Arabic lettering and the value in a simple engraved frame, with no portrait.

name: Great Sphinx of Giza
file: File:Sphinx in front of Cheops pyramid 1M.jpg
description: Egyptian stamp of 1888 showing the Sphinx before the Great Pyramid.
story: This 1M value from the 1888 emission puts the Sphinx in front of the Great Pyramid - an early example of Egypt using its monuments on ordinary postage rather than reserving them for commemoratives.
designNote: Stone and desert as flat tonal bands, keeping the pyramid's outline sharp.

name: Egyptian Revolution of 1952
description: Egyptian stamp commemorating the revolution of 23 July 1952.
story: Army officers overthrew the monarchy on 23 July 1952, and Egypt later marked the date on its postage. The issue turns a single day's events into the country's own annual commemoration.
designNote: A date-led commemorative design with a simple graphic device.

name: Kenya Independence
description: 1963 stamp showing Jomo Kenyatta facing Mount Kenya, cost 30 cents.
story: Kenya became independent on 12 December 1963 with Jomo Kenyatta as its first prime minister. This stamp, showing him before Mount Kenya, belongs to the country's opening issues as a new state.
designNote: Portrait and mountain paired across a wide format, printed in a single colour.

name: Royal Lion
description: 1938 Kenya-Uganda-Tanganyika issue pairing King George VI with a lion.
story: This 1938 issue pairs the king's portrait with a lion, and stamps like it are how many collectors first met the fauna of East Africa. The three colonies ran a shared post until independence.
designNote: The king's head in an oval beside a standing lion, in the engraved colonial style.

name: Chambered Nautilus
file: File:Stamp of Kenya - 1974 - Colnect 497001 - Chambered Nautilus Nautilus pompilius.jpeg
description: Kenyan issue of 1974 featuring the chambered nautilus.
story: Nautilus pompilius is a living fossil - a coiled shellfish whose lineage reaches back hundreds of millions of years - and it swims in the waters off East Africa. Kenya's 1974 wildlife issue put it on a stamp.
designNote: The spiral shell drawn in section, which is what makes the species read instantly at small size.
